dedupe_keys.name: fractracker national energy and petrochemical infrastructure map us 2021 update

description: This interactive map brings together public datasets on oil, gas and petrochemical infrastructure in the United States, from extraction to processing and transport, with each layer's facility count and update date listed. Layers include, for example, 30 ethylene crackers, 136 petroleum refineries, 99 crude oil rail terminals and 8 liquefied natural gas terminals from the Energy Information Administration, and natural gas compressor stations from the Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data, with a separate Excel list of retired power plants. It was built by the FracTracker Alliance, first released in February 2020 and updated in April 2021, with an article by Erica Jackson dated 30 June 2021. Coverage is national. The map and its source list are free to view online, with some layers downloadable; the part of the page read states no licence. Caveats: it is a compilation of other agencies' data, several layers had not been updated since the first release, and nothing newer than 2021 was seen, so it is marked stale. For simulation it shows how refineries, crackers, terminals and pipelines cluster, useful for hazard exposure and network studies of petrochemical supply chains; current layers should be taken from the original sources. It is related to the Spatial Finance Initiative GeoAsset databases record in this catalogue, which covers ethylene plants worldwide.
